subject: Service update — Dedicated capacity surge, remediation plan & committed actions
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: Dedicated capacity surge affecting your reserved pool — initial steps

Hi Elena,

I’m reaching out because we detected a sustained surge in utilization on the dedicated GPU pool backing Acme Corp’s reserved capacity beginning ~08:45 PST this morning. That surge pushed queuing and longer tails for some of your playback and long-context generation routes.

What we’ve done so far (first 45 minutes):
- Throttled lower-priority background jobs across the pool to free headroom for customer-facing routes.
- Applied a temporary autoscale override to bring additional reserved nodes online (this mitigated but did not fully eliminate long-tail latency).
- Redirected a small percentage of low-critical traffic to the warm fallback model to maintain throughput.

Immediate ask: can we schedule a 30-minute war room at 10:00 PST so our infra and your ops can align on impact and next steps? Marcus and Monica from our infra/ops teams will join.

I realize the impact is unacceptable during a business window — we own this and will follow up with a remediation plan and credit recommendation as soon as we have the RCA.

Attachments: heapdump-2028-06-11.log (extracted trace), capacity-plan-v2.pdf (initial mitigation checklist)

Sincerely,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147
From: Elena Torres <ops@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 10:05:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Dedicated capacity surge affecting your reserved pool — initial steps

Thanks Naomi — we’re seeing elevated errors and timeouts in Production. Appreciate the quick mitigations.

Quick questions:
1) Can you confirm whether any customer traffic was routed to multi-tenant hosts during the surge? We need a clear boundary for compliance reporting.
2) Please include an estimate for service credits and a proposed timeline for a full bounce-free recovery.

We can join the 10:00 PST call — I’ll have our SRE lead (internal) there.

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Corp
ops@acme-corp.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 11:30:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity surge — remediation plan & customer comms

Team — forwarding the thread with Acme. Summary from war room: root cause appears to be a combination of an orchestration race during autoscale where delayed scheduler acknowledgements caused simultaneous node addition and a misapplied global preemption threshold. The result: transient oversubscription on the reserved pool control plane, which increased queueing and triggered fallback routing logic in a narrow window.

Proposed next steps (internal):
- Patch: remove the global preemption override and add a conservative backoff window in the scheduler (INF-7812). Target deploy: 2028-06-12 02:00 UTC.
- Capacity: pre-warm two reserve nodes to hedge for similar spikes until we deploy the scheduler backoff (48h).
- Customer comms: confirm whether we route any Acme traffic to multi-tenant hosts (see Elena’s question) — if yes, prepare a compliance statement.
- Credits: propose a 15% service credit for the affected 36-hour window; draft attached for legal review.

I’ll assemble a short customer note and a formal post-incident timeline after we validate the patch in staging. Marcus, please validate the credit calc and confirm whether we can meet the 02:00 UTC deploy. Monica, coordinate legal and billing for the credit doc. Karthik, own the scheduler patch and the canary rollout plan.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity surge — remediation commitments and next steps

Elena,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Below is a concise remediation and compensation commitment from Redwood. We want to be explicit so Acme has a clear audit trail.

What happened (short): an orchestration timing issue during autoscale plus an overly-aggressive preemption threshold caused temporary oversubscription in your reserved pool’s control plane, which led to prolonged queuing for a subset of long-context generation requests between 08:45–10:20 PST on 2028-06-11. No customer traffic was routed to multi-tenant hosts at any point — the fallback path used warm fallback instances within your reserved capacity only.

Immediate technical actions completed:
- Disabled the preemption override and applied a scheduler backoff (canary run) — INF-7812 — canary showed stable behavior within 2 hours.
- Pre-warmed two reserved nodes and adjusted autoscale thresholds to avoid triggering simultaneous node adds.
- Added additional tracing around scheduler ACKs and queue depth metrics; logs collected and attached (heapdump-2028-06-11.log).

Planned actions and timeline:
- 2028-06-12 02:00 UTC: Rolling deploy of scheduler backoff to production (target + monitored rollback window).
- 2028-06-12 to 2028-06-14: Maintain the two pre-warmed nodes while we observe 48h of steady state.
- 2028-06-18: Post-incident review (internal) and customer-facing postmortem to be shared the next business day.

Compensation proposal:
- One-time service credit equal to 15% of Acme’s billable usage for the affected 36-hour window (2028-06-11 07:00 UTC – 2028-06-12 19:00 UTC). Attached: service-credits-commitment.pdf (draft). Please review and let us know if that aligns with your procurement/finance labelling needs.

Attachments: service-credits-commitment.pdf (draft), capacity-plan-v2.pdf (finalized mitigation checklist), heapdump-2028-06-11.log (collected traces)

Links:
- Internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7812
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HS-98765

If this is acceptable, we will send a formal DocuSign for the credit agreement and the customer-facing post-incident timeline on 2028-06-13.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
